newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian-based Palestinians hold talks in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Syrian-based Palestinians hold talks in Iraq.

text.p: The Syrian-based Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) said on Tuesday it had held talks with Iraq on the Middle East peace process and how to improve Baghdad's ties with Damascus and the Arab world.
The PFLP said in a statement that deputy leader Abu Ali Mustafa led a delegation to Iraq this month for talks with Vice President Taha Yassin Ramadan and Foreign Minister Tareq Aziz.

"Both sides asserted the necessity to create a correct atmosphere between Arabs...and to achieve an Arab-Arab reconciliation...that provides the basis for Arab solidarity to face the American-Israeli aggression.
"The Iraqi officials showed a positive position towards the ideas of the Front regarding the correct and healthy atmosphere between Syria and Iraq," the radical group added.

Ties between Syria and Iraq were cut off before the 1980s but representatives from the two sides met in Syria and Iraq this year to coordinate policies over a row with Turkey on sharing water from the Euphrates.

The statement said the PFLP team went to Iraq because of "the feeling of responsibility towards the Arab causes...and to put an end to the unjust embargo imposed on the brother Iraq and to break it with an Arab decision."
The United Nations imposed tough sanctions on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in 1990.
The PFLP said Iraqi officials "assured the firm Iraqi position to support the Palestinian revolution and their right to fight the Zionist occupation."
The PFLP belongs to a 10-member alliance based in Damascus that has vowed to wreck the PLO-Israeli peace deal for self-rule in Gaza and the West Bank.
